search_row.title: Twofold cost of sex
search_row.statement: An asexual mutant female in a sexual population with equal sex ratio produces twice as many grandchildren as a sexual female, so sex needs a compensating advantage of up to twofold to persist.
search_row.math: with equal fecundity and a 1:1 sex ratio, the odds of asexual to sexual females double each generation: \frac{q_{t+1}}{1-q_{t+1}} = 2\frac{q_t}{1-q_t}

fields.dct:source: John Maynard Smith (1978) The Evolution of Sex
fields.delphi:proposedTest: In a species with coexisting sexual and asexual lineages, measure relative per-capita growth of asexual versus sexual females in a common environment and compare it with the predicted factor of 2.
fields.delphi:context: Assumptions: anisogamy with males contributing no resources, equal fecundity and viability of sexual and asexual females, a 1:1 sex ratio. Formal status: proved as a population-dynamic identity under these assumptions. Its biological force depends on how often those assumptions hold.
